newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 28.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- The Bank of Korea said South Korea's corporate efficiency was too low. Korea lags Japan by 14 years in terms of added value ratio, uses energy four times more than Japan for the same amount of output.
- Government, ruling New Korea party decide to entrust foreign companies with job of conducting inspection of high-speed railway projects.

- The government and the ruling New Korea party are weighing a plan to create a "political cabinet" by installing a number of government party lawmakers as cabinet members, including the post of Prime Minister. This is meant to strengthen the administration's responsibility during the latter part of president Kim's tenure.
- North Korea beefs up its air force, securing 30 more MiG-19s for a total of 160, according to the International Institute of Strategic Studies.

- Former Defense Minister Lee Yang-ho has been questioned for the source of funds million he used to buy bonds in connection with investigation of his alleged involvement in bribery scandal linked with combat helicopter contract.
- North Korea will offer a sweeping bid to improve relations with the U.S., recognizing the presence of U.S. troops in S. Korea, according to a Beijing source familiar with North Korean affairs.
- Call-back service phone cards illegally distributed to about 50,000 to 60,000 Koreans who use the cards for calls to U.S. at 50 to 60 percent lower rate than existing rates in Korea.
